s: A cement quarry reborn as a wildlife park
w: Bamburi's old limestone quarry, stripped raw by cement mining, was rebuilt into a nature park where giraffes, hippos and buffalo now graze reclaimed ground. Its best-known residents were Owen and Mzee, a hippo and a giant tortoise whose friendship made this park a fixture of wildlife headlines until March 2007.

s: A museum built inside Kenya's first church
w: This museum occupies the very building where missionaries Johann Ludwig Krapf and Johannes Rebmann raised Kenya's first Christian church. Most of what fills its rooms traces Krapf's own work here - the modest chapel from which Christian mission spread along Kenya's coast and beyond.

n: Mombasa Marine National Park and Reserve
s: Kenya's most-visited stretch of protected reef
w: Coral gardens just offshore make this Kenya's most frequently visited marine park, a protected reef and reserve covering more than 200 square kilometres of coast. Snorkellers and divers drift over crabs, starfish and turtles while crab plovers work the tideline - a whole reef ecosystem within sight of the mainland.
